schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: One parse of every .py file in the tree into an import graph, and the sieves that shake it. Three primitives: `import_graph(root)` — {relpath: every dotted name it imports}; `importers_of(graph, path)` — who imports the module at this path, the question the ruling door asks before letting a packet sentence a file; `catches(graph, rule)` — shake one sieve and return what its MESH caught. THREE rule kinds, because the corpus asks three different questions: `sole_path` (these modules may be imported ONLY from inside this prefix — the domain chokepoint), `forbidden` (this prefix may not import these at all — a fork, so one thing survives the other breaking), and SINCE 2026-08-12 `unreachable` (nothing `start` can REACH may reach these — ticket reachability-replaces-the-allowlist). The third is a different SHAPE, not a third filter: the first two ask about ONE HOP and can be answered by reading a file, while `unreachable` asks about the whole path and can only be answered by WALKING it, which is why it needed a new primitive — `reaches(graph, start)` returns every file `start` arrives at by any number of import hops, each with its shortest chain, and it is `importers_of` run forwards and transitively rather than backwards and once. The kind exists because the alternative it replaced does not scale: an ALLOWLIST of what a path may import has to be widened by hand every time the corpus grows a legitimate dependency, and the widening is a decision nobody records — measured 2026-08-12, `cairn.tools.base.nest` entered the build_inspector fire path in 047d633 without it, so a tooth that was not holding read as one that was. Naming the DENIED CAPABILITY is what makes a rule general: the innocent never need signatures. A finding carries the whole route (`a -> b -> c`), because a breach reported without its chain sends the reader back to re-derive how the path got there. AND SINCE 2026-08-06, REACH: `reach_of(source)` — {function: band}, how far each function in a module has to look to answer, resolved through what its aliases actually IMPORT rather than what its calls are spelled. THE ASSEMBLY AND THE VOCABULARY LEFT 2026-08-07 (ruling 2026-08-07-the-nest-is-block-general, ticket banding-berths-at-the-general-level): `nest(reaches)` and `BAND_NAMES` now live at `cairn/tools/base/nest.py`, because a band's MEANING is block-general and the assembly berths where any tenant can reach it; what stays HERE is DERIVATION — `reach_of` and the ladder — because how a band is computed for an import-shaped sieve is this component's own craft. The ladder (DEFAULT_LADDER) is DATA and a first cut: in-hand / local-disk / correlated-local / off-box, boundaries drawn where the FAILURE MODE changes rather than where the milliseconds do.
why: Five artifacts had been standing on the sentence 'enforced by the tester import-scan once that tooth exists' since 2026-07-18 — db_domain's falsifier (4), inference_domain's falsifier (6), intentions_model_compiler, CLAUDE.md's rules-awaiting-physics list, and a ruling packet whose own line read 'Guarded by import-scan, never by prose'. That last one is the why in one image: the sentence asserting the rule was not prose was itself the only thing enforcing it (Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics; until it is, it is a tracked debt). THE LIVED SYMPTOM the last customer fixes: on 2026-08-05 two ruling packets sentenced cairn/tools/base/probe.py — the Probe primitive — to deletion while 19 live modules imported it. Akien was one `cairn ruling confirm` away from making 'delete the file the corpus is built on' a green instruction, and the confirm screen shows him the READING, which was correct; nothing showed him the kill list. Both packets were caught by hand, which is the wrong mechanism twice over. THE REACH HALF (ticket the-questions-are-the-sieve, 2026-08-06) is the same lesson arriving a third time. Akien: coarseness is 'not computation time... more like how deep we have to look... more related to proximity?' A first cut of the derivation matched call-name tails and put 15 of build_inspector's 18 checks off-box, because Path.resolve() and inference_domain.resolve() share a tail — mention-not-capability, in a new shape, caught by measurement rather than by memory. It lives here rather than in build_inspector because a sieve's band is a characteristic of the KIND OF THING it does, not of where it is installed, which is what makes a sieve portable between nests (Akien: 'greater reusability'). It is NOT part of import_graph because that graph is MODULE-granular and a sieve is a FUNCTION: inspector.py imports pathlib once and holds eighteen checks with different reaches.
invoke: import: `from cairn.tools.import_sieve import sieve`. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve.py` (exit 0 = green). Consumers declare their own rule at their own address — db_domain/proofs/test_sole_path.py, inference_domain/proofs/test_host.py, cairn/machines/ruling/ruling.py.
node_class: primitive (a library, not a device) — it owns no resource and has no face. It is read-only over the tree and returns findings; nothing here decides what to do about them. TODAY it also keeps nothing between calls, which is a fact about this build and not a property of toolhood: ruling 2026-08-14-tools-and-machines-remember-under-their-holder settles that a tool MAY carry state and history, berthed under the holder that assembled it, and it stays the holder's to own and gate.
entry: FRESH code, PROVEN pattern, promoted rather than invented. The design is inference_domain's own sole-path tooth — AST-parsed, outbound-only, matched on full dotted names, with a non-hollow floor — generalized and moved once so it stops being one component's private habit. Its two hard-won mesh lessons came from the corpus and are built in: learning_block's tooth grepped whole source and fired on its own honest docstring, fixed by scoping to import lines; inference_domain's grepped the host's port and API paths and fired on cairn/tools/base/needs.py where ':11434/api/tags' appears in a docstring, an error message and a fixture, fixed by testing the CAPABILITY rather than the mention. Nothing crossed from outside Cairn.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why
the_mesh_is_the_whole_difficulty: A sieve is only as good as its ability to tell a capability from a mention of one, and the corpus has now taught that three times. `urllib.parse.parse_qs` is string work and no more a door than `str.split`; `urllib.request` is a door — a word-matching scan cannot separate them and web_server/server.py is the live file it would red on day one. `http.server` LISTENS; a dial rule that catches it reds the one component whose whole job is to be reachable. And a fixture STRING containing 'from cairn.tools.base.probe import Probe' is data, not an import — measured 2026-08-06, grep counted 23 carriers of probe.py where the sieve counts 19, and all four of the difference are prose or fixtures. Hence: parse with ast, match full dotted names, never ask whether a word appears.
filed_edges: (a) A SUBPROCESS IS INVISIBLE. `subprocess.run(['curl', ...])` dials and imports nothing; so does a dynamic `importlib.import_module(computed_name)`. Every sole-path green here means 'no second door BY IMPORT', which is narrower than 'no second door'. Named rather than papered over — a green read wider than it is measured is the failure this component exists to end.

(b) THE FIFTH CUSTOMER DISSOLVED RATHER THAN BEING SERVED, AND THAT IS THE HONEST RECORD. Four of the five IOUs this component was built for closed on 2026-08-06. The fifth — intentions_model_compiler's 'no second WRITER of intentions-congruency-lab/' — was never servable here (a write is a verb, not an import) and briefly stood as a write-scan owed. Akien then ruled the premise away the same day: the lab is a viewing surface and several derived writers are legitimate, so the invariant is derived-never-authored and the tooth it needs is a conformance check over the FOLDER, not a scan over code at all. No write-scan is owed to this component or to anyone. Ticket the-lab-is-derived-never-authored.

(c) RELATIVE IMPORTS RESOLVE TO NOTHING. `from . import x` is skipped rather than resolved to an absolute name. Measured 2026-08-06: the corpus contains zero relative imports, so this is a real hole with no current occupant. It becomes a defect the day someone writes one.

(d) NOBODY SHAKES THE NEST. Each rule lives at its owner's address and fires under that owner's proof, which is correct (Law 5 — the constraint beside the thing it protects) and means there is no single place that reports every sole-path at once. That is a view, not an owner, and it should stay a view; when the frontier projector exists this is one of its inputs.

(e) NO CACHE, BY CHOICE. The graph is rebuilt per call — 200 files, milliseconds. A cached graph would be a scan reporting on a corpus that no longer exists, which is precisely the failure mode being closed.

(reach-a) A BAND SEQUENCES, IT NEVER FORBIDS — Akien's correction 2026-08-06, after CC proposed a tooth redding any off-box sieve in the build gate on the ground that none exists today. There are already two hosts (this box and Hex), and in TheIgors era four laptops each carried a copy of the database and ran an instance with four centers of awareness against local 3b/7b Ollama on ten-minute overnight timeouts. His words: 'will we do that? I don't know. but we CAN.' So the off-box band's job is that a distant sieve runs LAST and an unreachable host cannot mask a local finding. THE BAND IS EMPTY TODAY AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A RULE — measured over the 18 live checks, 2026-08-06.

(reach-b) THE LADDER IS A FIRST CUT AND EXPECTED TO WIDEN. It was derived from the eighteen checks that existed on 2026-08-06 and the sorting pass found THREE of its four bands populated — 13 of 18 in correlated-local, so the domain is flatter than the metaphor and fine-grained ordering buys little today. What earns its keep is the COARSE band as a precondition gate (a component with no charter currently emits thirteen findings about its chart packets) and the off-box boundary as sequencing. A subprocess still dials invisibly — the header's standing caveat applies to reach exactly as it applies to the graph.

(reach-c) CLOSED IN TWO ACTS, and the second act moved the furniture. 2026-08-06: build_inspector's banding landed and `reach_of` found its consumer — tenant #1 derives its nest through it on every inspection (ticket the-questions-are-the-sieve child (a)). 2026-08-07: `nest` itself LEFT — ruling 2026-08-07-the-nest-is-block-general lifted the assembly and the shake to `cairn/tools/base/nest.py` (ticket banding-berths-at-the-general-level), so 'nothing consumes them' is false on one half and the other half no longer lives here. The not-applicable rule (a sieve stopped by a coarser band is ABSENT from the report, never 0.0) is built into the gradation's SHAPE at the general berth and no suppression is wired, because no measured case wants one (build_inspector edge nest-b).
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_import_sieve.py, run by the tester. Every catching tooth is PAIRED: the same rule shaken over a planted graph (must catch) and over the real corpus (must not), because either half alone is satisfied by a sieve made of solid sheet metal.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a mention becomes a catch — a docstring, comment or fixture string naming a module is reported as importing it; (2) a capability escapes the mesh — urllib.request or psycopg2 imported outside its domain and NOT caught; (3) a sieve shaken over a tree it did not read reports clean instead of raising HollowScan (Law 8 — a green over zero files is not a green); (4) `importers_of` returns [] for a file that live modules import, which is the exact condition under which a ruling packet may sentence it to death; (5) an unknown rule kind returns clean rather than raising — a typo'd rule that passes forever is worse than no rule.
how_it_learns: It doesn't, and the reason is the point: this is a MESH, and a mesh that adapts is not a measurement. Its rules are declared by the components that own the constraint and change only when a human rules that the constraint changed. What DOES learn is the mesh's precision, and it learns the way Cairn's other gates do — by firing wrongly once and being narrowed, with the correction written into the code as a permanent trap rather than into someone's memory. Three such narrowings are already carried as teeth (whole-source→import-lines, port-literal→capability, word-match→full-dotted-name), each one a false red that a human adjudicated. If a fourth false red appears, the answer is a new paired tooth, never a loosened assertion.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — this is the tooth five IOUs were waiting on, and the debt was tracked as an IOU exactly as the law requires)
Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — the sole-path scan existed in one component's proof and was about to be re-derived in a second; it lives once instead)
Law 6 (exactly one owner — a sole path IS the owner's gate; a second importer is a second door, and the gate's whole claim is that there is one)
Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — the HollowScan raise is that law aimed at this component's own green)
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — 'sole by construction' was a claim about the present that nothing re-checked)
owner: CC owns import_sieve's code and proofs and gates writes to them. Each RULE is owned by the component whose constraint it is — db_domain owns the 5432 mesh, inference_domain owns the dial mesh — and lives at that component's address, not here. There is deliberately no central rule registry (no-enforcer, gated ownership).
gated_by_why: DERIVED FROM `owner` ABOVE BY THE RULE `owner` ITSELF STATES, and filled 2026-08-12 at the moment a real crossing needed it (ticket reachability-replaces-the-allowlist, which would have refused at the clearance gate with OwnerUnresolvable at its own last step). The derivation is base's, authored on 2026-08-11 and quoted here rather than re-derived: gated_by names the hands the owner-gate admits, and `owner` says WHO GATES WRITES. This one says CC and only CC — Akien is not named as a write-gater here, and unlike cairn/tools/base this is not his artifact but a tooth built at his direction. That is harbor_master's shape exactly ('CC owns the code + proofs and gates writes to them' -> ["CC"]), and following it is the whole point: a field derived by a stated rule is checkable, one filled by feel is not. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: nothing here grants standing over any other intention's tickets, and nothing here decides who owns a RULE — the sentence above still binds, each rule belongs to the component whose constraint it is, and this list gates writes to THIS component's code and proofs. A MEASURED INCONSISTENCY, NAMED RATHER THAN COPIED: of the three charters carrying this field before today, cairn/tools/base and cairn/devices/harbor_master both derive it from their `owner` prose and say so; cairn/devices/ground_loop carries ["Akien", "CC"] with NO `gated_by_why` while its `owner` names only CC as write-gater. That entry is mine, added 2026-08-12 in dc3634f during a-record-reaches-disk, and it does not follow the rule base states. Whether Akien belongs in EVERY gated_by by Law 9 — or only where the `owner` prose puts him — is a real open question and it is filed at ticket an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands, where the fleet-wide fill already lives. It is not answered by this charter, and it was not answered by quietly matching the outlier.
proof: proofs/test_import_sieve.py — 28 teeth (measured 2026-08-12: 28/28 green; 15 at 2026-08-06, 20 after the reach bands, 28 with the walk). The mesh: a parse is not a dial; listening is not dialing; prose is not an import; an in-tree leaf import is visible; an unparseable file is not a door. The floor: a sieve over one file raises rather than passing, and the real corpus clears it. The catches: sole_path catches a planted second door and is clean on the real corpus for BOTH domains; forbidden catches a fork breach and spares everyone else; an unknown kind is refused. importers_of: finds the 19 live carriers of base/probe.py, returns [] for a module nobody imports, and a module is not its own importer. THE WALK (8 teeth, 2026-08-12) is paired for one MORE reason than the two kinds above: a walk that silently returns nothing is invisible from the passing side. So it pins all three ways it can be wrong — a breach TWO HOPS down that must be caught, a module that breaches identically OFF the path and must not be (the line between `unreachable` and `forbidden`), and HollowScan still raising for a kind written after it. Verified by running the whole file with `reaches` stubbed to return {}: five teeth fail there, including the real-corpus one, whose non-vacuity assert refuses to go green over an empty closure.
provenance: Built 2026-08-06 at Akien's direction — 'then it sounds like we do import-scan next' — the morning after a ruling pass in which the missing tooth surfaced twice: once as the gate troubles/what-dies-sentences-files-the-corpus-still-imports was owed, and once as a ruling packet claiming physics that measurably did not exist. The measurement that opened it: `import-scan` appeared nowhere in the corpus as code; every one of its occurrences was an IOU reading 'once that tooth exists'. Verified on the way in that the pattern was already proven in-house (inference_domain's tooth) rather than invented here, and on the way out with a live mutant probe planted at the skills/ root — missed by the old glob, caught by the sieve.
